title: His Father Sold Four Acres of Farmland in Madurai. On Friday, Selva Prabhu Won the NCAA Triple Jump Title.
excerpt: The 21-year-old Kansas State sophomore from Tamil Nadu became the first Indian to win an NCAA Outdoor title since Tejaswin Shankar in 2022, leaping 16.94 metres at Hayward Field in Eugene.
body:
The last time a Kansas State Wildcat won the NCAA Outdoor triple jump championship, Ronald Reagan was president and Halley's Comet was in the sky. Kenny Harrison took the title in 1986, and then forty years of silence followed.

On Friday evening at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon, a 21-year-old from Madurai named **Selva Prabhu Thirumaran** ended the wait.

Prabhu leaped 16.94 metres on his second attempt to top a 24-athlete field and win the 2026 NCAA Division I Outdoor triple jump title. He fouled four of his six jumps. The one that counted was enough.

"He just competed like the champion and the warrior that he is," Kansas State head coach Travis Geopfert said after the meet. "He went out there early, executed early, and won a national title for K-State."

## From a Doctor's Clinic in Madurai to Hayward Field

Prabhu's path to Eugene started in circumstances that would be familiar to many Indian families weighing a child's sporting ambition against financial reality. His father sold four acres of farmland to fund his son's dreams of competing at the highest level. The bet has paid off faster than anyone expected.

Prabhu arrived at Kansas State as a freshman in 2024 and finished fifth at his first NCAA Outdoor Championship with a jump of 16.09 metres. In January 2026, he opened his sophomore year at the Thane Baker Invite with a 16.49-metre effort that also cleared the Athletics Federation of India's Asian Games qualifying standard of 16.28 metres.

Then the season accelerated. In March, he won silver at the NCAA Indoor Championships in Fayetteville with a leap of 17.05 metres — a new Kansas State school record, breaking Vince Parrette's 1980 mark of 17.03 metres. In May, he won the Big 12 title at 17.19 metres, though a wind reading of 4.6 m/s prevented it from becoming an official record.

## India's Growing Footprint in American College Athletics

Prabhu's gold is India's first NCAA Outdoor title in four years. The last Indian to achieve the feat was high jumper Tejaswin Shankar, who won in 2022 (and previously in 2018). Together, they represent a small but growing pipeline of Indian track and field athletes training and competing in the American collegiate system.

The 2022 World Athletics U20 Championships in Cali, Colombia, was where Prabhu first announced himself internationally, winning a silver medal in the triple jump as a 17-year-old. That performance caught the attention of American college recruiters, and he enrolled at Kansas State shortly after.

His coach, Geopfert, noted that the programme now has two individual NCAA champions in the same season — Prabhu in the triple jump and Tah Chikomba in the long jump — a first in Kansas State history. The men's team finished eighth overall with 30 points, their best result since 1998.

## What Comes Next

Prabhu's next target is the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya later this year, though selection is not guaranteed. The Athletics Federation of India requires athletes to compete in at least three domestic meets, including mandatory state-level appearances, to be eligible. Having spent his season entirely in the United States, Prabhu may need to return to India to meet those criteria.

For now, the numbers tell a clean story: a personal best of 17.05 metres indoors, a wind-aided 17.19 outdoors, an NCAA title at 20, and a 40-year drought at Kansas State finally broken.

## A Wider Diaspora Story

Prabhu's journey mirrors a pattern that NRI families across the United States would recognise — a young athlete from a small city leveraging the American collegiate athletics system to reach heights that India's domestic infrastructure alone might not have enabled. Kansas State's Manhattan, Kansas, is not a traditional destination for Indian students, but Geopfert's track programme has built a reputation for developing international jumpers, having previously coached Carey McLeod and Jaydon Hibbert to NCAA titles at Arkansas.

For the Indian athletics community, the question now is whether Prabhu can bridge the gap between NCAA success and senior international competition. India's national record in the men's triple jump — 17.37 metres, held by Praveen Chithravel — is within reach. His indoor best of 17.05 metres is already closer than most Indian triple jumpers have ever been.

The four acres of farmland in Madurai bought more than anyone could have predicted.

*Sources: Kansas State Athletics, The Bridge, IANS, Wikipedia*
